description: Fan blade erosion detected on blades 12, 17, and 23 during routine 500-cycle visual inspection. Leading edge erosion depth measured at 0.030 in on blade 17, approaching the AMM blend repair limit of 0.040 in. Suspected cause is sand and grit ingestion during operations at arid-region airports over the previous 500 cycles.
action_taken: Performed blend repair on blades 12, 17, and 23 per AMM Chapter 72-21. Post-blend contour verified with inspection template. Fan assembly balance rechecked; no trim balance weight required. Borescope images documented in engine health record.

description: Mechanical seal on Pump-03 observed leaking at approximately 8 drops per minute at the gland plate, detected during shift walkdown. Rate significantly exceeds zero-leakage requirement for mechanical seal service. Process fluid is light naphtha, classified as hazardous and flammable. Seal had been in service 22,000 hours.
action_taken: Isolated pump using block valves. Drained and cooled casing. Removed mechanical seal assembly. Drive ring showed scoring across 20 percent of face width. Replaced complete John Crane Type 1 mechanical seal assembly. Verified shaft runout at 0.0015 in TIR. Zero leakage confirmed at operating pressure after restart.
parts_replaced: John Crane Type 1 mechanical seal assembly

description: Piston ring wear detected on Stage 1 cylinder of Comp-02 during scheduled 8000-hour overhaul. End gap on all four compression rings exceeded acceptance criteria: Ring 1 at 0.020 in, Ring 2 at 0.019 in, Ring 3 at 0.021 in, Ring 4 at 0.017 in (maximum allowable 0.018 in). Blowby measured at 4.8 percent, just below the 5 percent limit.
action_taken: Disassembled Stage 1 cylinder. Withdrew piston assembly. Removed all four worn rings and two rider rings. Installed new PTFE-filled piston rings with end gaps staggered at 120 degrees. Verified ring side clearance 0.002 in. Reinstalled piston with new O-rings and cylinder head gasket. Interstage temperature stable at 295 degrees F after 24-hour post-restart monitoring.
parts_replaced: Stage 1 piston ring set (4 compression rings)

description: Oil pressure low alert on Engine-07 during cruise at FL350. ECAM displayed low oil pressure warning at 28 PSIG, below normal minimum of 35 PSIG. Crew performed precautionary power reduction. Engine continued to operate with pressure slightly below limit. Post-flight inspection initiated at maintenance base.
action_taken: Found oil level at minimum mark. Oil pump output tested at 38 PSIG (degraded from nominal 52 PSIG). Inspected oil filter; found moderate metallic debris. Replaced oil filter element and refilled oil to maximum level. Post-refill pump test: 52 PSIG. Borescoped accessible bearing areas; no unusual wear observed. Engine returned to service with enhanced monitoring.

description: Suction strainer on Pump-07 found blocked during operator rounds. Differential pressure across strainer basket measured at 4.5 psi, above the 2.0 psi blockage limit. Pump experienced reduced flow (780 GPM versus design 1,100 GPM) and elevated vibration due to near-cavitation conditions. Root cause was debris from upstream piping work performed the previous week.
action_taken: Shut down pump and transferred service to standby Pump-08. Found basket completely clogged with mill scale, pipe debris, and fibrous material. Cleaned basket with high-pressure water and air. Reinstalled and restarted. Post-cleaning differential pressure 0.3 psi. Flow rate returned to 1,095 GPM.

description: Vibration anomaly detected on Engine-05 during routine engine health monitoring review. N1 channel vibration trending data shows a gradual increase over the past 200 flight cycles, rising from a baseline of 0.22 in/s to a current reading of 0.54 in/s, which exceeds the 0.5 in/s WARNING threshold. The trend is smooth and progressive, suggesting developing imbalance or early-stage LP bearing wear rather than a discrete FOD event. No crew reports of abnormal noise or handling.
action_taken: Reduced power setting by 5 percent per standing instructions for vibration in WARNING band. Performed visual inspection of all 38 fan blades; no visible damage or erosion beyond normal. Borescope performed on fan and LPC Stage 1; no anomalies found. Oil sample submitted to laboratory for metals analysis. Enhanced vibration monitoring initiated with readings every 10 flight hours. Follow-up borescope scheduled within 25 flight hours.

description: Intercooler fouling identified on Comp-05 during quarterly performance check. Gas-side pressure drop measured at 7.2 psi, significantly above the 5.0 psi clean baseline. Interstage temperature was 340 degrees F, exceeding the design approach temperature. Tube fouling suspected due to hard water deposits and biological growth in the cooling water circuit.
action_taken: Isolated intercooler and drained both sides. Borescoped tubes; confirmed heavy calcium carbonate scale. Circulated 10 percent citric acid solution at 2 GPM for 4 hours at 120 degrees F. Flushed with clean water until pH neutral. Post-cleaning pressure drop 3.8 psi. Interstage temperature returned to 305 degrees F. Reinstalled with new channel cover gaskets.

description: Foreign object damage to Engine-12 fan reported following bird strike during approach to landing. Flight crew reported a single loud bang and brief vibration increase at 2,000 ft AGL during approach. Vibration returned to near-normal quickly. Engine shut down after landing per procedure. Preliminary visual inspection through inlet revealed damage to several fan blades.
action_taken: Detailed borescope of fan: blade 8 with dent 0.045 in depth (exceeds blend limit of 0.040 in), blade 9 with bent tip, blade 10 with nick within blend limits. Replaced blades 8 and 9 with serviceable units. Blended blade 10 per AMM. Re-balanced fan assembly with one 0.5 oz trim balance weight. Post-repair ground run vibration: 0.28 in/s. Engine returned to service.

description: Bearing overheating fault detected on Pump-11 by continuous temperature monitoring system. Bearing housing temperature reached 92 degrees C (normal maximum 70 degrees C above ambient). Pump was running at design flow rate. Oil level appeared low in sight glass. Vibration showed slight increase from baseline, suggesting bearing deterioration.
action_taken: Shut down Pump-11 and transferred service to spare Pump-12. Drained oil; found dark and oxidized with metallic smell. Removed bearings; SKF 6309 radial bearing showed spalling on outer raceway. Replaced both radial and thrust bearing sets. Flushed housing and refilled with fresh ISO VG 68 oil (1.2 quarts). Bearing temperature stable at 58 degrees C after 2 hours.

description: Rod packing leakage detected on Stage 2 cylinder piston rod of Comp-08 during operator walkdown. Gas leakage visible as white mist from packing case vent. Leakage rate estimated at 5 standard cubic feet per minute, above acceptable limit. Packing had been in service for approximately 6,500 hours.
action_taken: Shut down and depressurized compressor. Removed cylinder head and stuffing box gland. Extracted all 5 packing rings; rings were heavily worn with 35 percent height reduction. Piston rod surface showed minor polishing but no scoring. Installed new 5-ring PTFE chevron packing set, lightly oiled before installation. Torqued gland to 65 ft-lb. Pressurized slowly and confirmed leakage eliminated.
parts_replaced: Stage 2 rod packing ring set (5 rings)

description: Early indication of LP shaft bearing distress on Engine-15 detected through routine oil analysis at 1000-cycle inspection. Sample shows elevated iron at 185 ppm (normal less than 50 ppm) and copper at 68 ppm, consistent with bearing cage and babbitt wear. Vibration on N1 channel at 0.41 in/s, slightly elevated from previous reading of 0.28 in/s 50 cycles ago. No ECAM bearing alerts yet but metals trend is strongly upward.
action_taken: Flagged engine for enhanced monitoring. Oil sample frequency increased to every 50 cycles. Vibration monitoring increased to every 5 flight hours. Notified airline technical operations and CFM field service representative. Reviewed FADEC fault history; N1 speed micro-variations recorded twice in last 200 cycles. Placed engine on watch list for early removal recommendation. Engine continues in service pending engineering review.

description: Coupling misalignment detected on Pump-05 during quarterly vibration survey. Vibration measured at 3.8 mm/s RMS at pump outboard bearing housing (warning threshold 2.3 mm/s). Vibration spectrum showed dominant peak at 1x running speed (3,600 CPM), classic signature of parallel misalignment. Pump had been reinstalled 3 months prior following impeller replacement without a properly documented alignment check.
action_taken: Shut down pump and locked out motor. Measured alignment with dial indicator: parallel offset 0.0065 in (limit 0.002 in), angular 0.0030 in/in (limit 0.001 in/in). Adjusted motor using jackscrews and shims to parallel 0.0008 in, angular 0.0004 in/in. Replaced worn coupling insert. Post-alignment vibration: 1.4 mm/s RMS. Alignment data logged in equipment file.

description: Suction valve failure detected on Stage 1 of Comp-11. Capacity dropped from rated 1,000 CFM to approximately 820 CFM. Stage 1 discharge temperature increased 18 degrees F above normal, indicating gas recirculation through a leaking suction valve. Stage 1 suction valve temperature monitoring showed 185 degrees F versus normal 140 degrees F.
action_taken: Shut down compressor and isolated. Removed all four Stage 1 suction valve assemblies. Disassembly revealed fractured valve plate on valve S1-B; plate cracked through three concentric rings. All four suction valve plate and spring sets replaced. Seat flatness checked; all within 0.002 in. Reinstalled with new O-rings, torqued to 85 ft-lb. Performance test confirmed capacity 995 CFM.
parts_replaced: Stage 1 suction valve plate set (4 valves)

description: Combustion instability detected on Engine-03 via FADEC fault recording during climb. EGT probe spread of 55 degrees C between highest and lowest probes (normal spread less than 30 degrees C). Fuel nozzle clogging suspected; Engine-03 had been operating in dusty environments for 400 cycles since last 500-cycle inspection.
action_taken: Removed 5 fuel nozzles by rotation schedule for bench flow test. Two nozzles found with 15 percent and 22 percent flow reduction due to carbonaceous deposits. Cleaned all 5 with approved ultrasonic cleaning solution. Borescoped combustion liner through all 20 ports; two minor hot spots documented within acceptable limits. EGT spread reduced to 18 degrees C after reinstallation.

description: High vibration alarm triggered on Pump-09 at 4.8 mm/s RMS, exceeding the CRITICAL threshold of 4.5 mm/s per ISO 10816-3. Vibration spectrum showed dominant 2x running speed frequency with sub-synchronous 0.8x component, characteristic of impeller imbalance combined with partial cavitation. Pump was operating at 100 percent design flow.
action_taken: Initiated controlled shutdown and transferred service to Pump-10. Found approximately 2.0 g of material missing from suction surface of impeller vane 7 due to cavitation damage. Replaced impeller with new unit, dynamically balanced to G2.5. Checked pump to motor alignment. Post-restart vibration: 1.8 mm/s RMS. Raised suction vessel level by 2 ft to improve NPSHa margin.

description: High discharge temperature alarm on Stage 2 of Comp-04. Measured discharge temperature 335 degrees F, exceeding maximum allowable 300 degrees F. Cooling water inlet temperature normal at 78 degrees F. Reduced cooling water flow was identified as the likely cause.
action_taken: Measured cooling water flow at Stage 2 cylinder outlet: only 9 GPM versus minimum 15 GPM. Found a partially closed isolation valve left 40 percent closed following recent piping maintenance. Fully opened valve; cooling water flow increased to 18 GPM. Stage 2 discharge temperature dropped to 288 degrees F within 20 minutes. Inspected Stage 2 discharge valves; all plates intact. Root cause documented as operator error.

description: Bleed valve stuck fault recorded on Engine-18 FADEC during descent at FL150. FADEC detected high-pressure bleed valve failed to open during deceleration, causing abnormal HPC pressure ratio and slight N1 speed fluctuation. FADEC attempted three auto-reset cycles without success. Post-landing maintenance investigation initiated.
action_taken: Accessed bleed valve assembly through lower cowl. Found pneumatic actuator stuck due to carbon buildup on valve stem from oil mist contamination. Removed valve assembly. Cleaned valve stem and actuator bore with approved carbon solvent. Lubricated sliding surfaces with high-temp dry lubricant per CMM. Cycled valve manually 20 times. Ground run confirmed full valve cycle without FADEC fault. Returned to service.

description: Oil contamination in bearing housing of Pump-13 discovered during monthly oil level check. Oil appeared milky white, a definitive indicator of water contamination. Laboratory confirmed water content 0.18 percent, exceeding maximum allowable 0.05 percent. Water ingress source was a nearby cooling water pipe spray leak directing water onto the bearing housing vent.
action_taken: Drained contaminated oil. Flushed housing three times with Shell Risella 46 flushing oil. Removed both bearings; radial bearing showed early white rust on inner ring raceway. Replaced both bearings as precaution. Repaired cooling water pipe spray leak by replacing flange gasket. Rerouted bearing housing vent away from water sources. Refilled with fresh ISO VG 68 oil. Post-restart 100-hour oil sample confirmed water below 0.01 percent.

description: Lube oil contamination discovered during 1,000-hour oil analysis on Comp-07. Silicon at 48 ppm (maximum 10 ppm), indicating airborne contamination. Iron was 280 ppm (normal less than 100 ppm). Particle count was ISO 19/17/13, significantly exceeding ISO 16/14/11 limit. Inlet air filter element was found torn, allowing unfiltered air into crankcase breather.
action_taken: Drained crankcase. Replaced torn inlet air filter element. Flushed entire oil system by circulating flushing oil via oil pump for 30 minutes. Changed oil filter element. Refilled with fresh ISO VG 68 oil. Inspected accessible main bearings through inspection covers; all within clearance limits. Re-sampled at 100 hours: silicon 4 ppm, iron 55 ppm, particle count ISO 14/12/9.

description: Fuel flow sensor fault recorded by FADEC on Engine-09. Erratic fuel flow readings fluctuating plus or minus 8 percent around mean value, well outside the acceptable plus or minus 2 percent tolerance. Fault persisted through two FADEC reset attempts. FADEC switched to alternate fuel scheduling mode; engine performance unaffected but accurate monitoring compromised.
action_taken: Accessed Coriolis-type fuel flow sensor on fuel supply manifold. Sensor failed internal diagnostics via FADEC maintenance menu. Measured sensor resistance; confirmed internal open circuit failure. Replaced sensor with calibrated replacement. Verified new sensor deviation less than 0.8 percent against aircraft fuel quantity data. FADEC reverted to primary scheduling mode. Post-installation functional test confirmed all parameters normal.

description: Follow-up inspection of Engine-05 vibration anomaly (originally logged WO-10079, March 2023). Vibration has progressed from 0.54 in/s at first detection to 0.76 in/s at current measurement â€” still within WARNING band but with a continued upward trend over 200 flight cycles. Oil sample returns elevated iron at 142 ppm and copper at 45 ppm, consistent with LP bearing cage wear. FADEC data shows intermittent N1 speed micro-variation at 1 Hz, suggesting bearing race defect frequency. Combined indicators point to developing LP bearing failure.
action_taken: Reduced thrust output limit to 93 percent N1 maximum per precautionary operating restriction. Performed full borescope of fan, LPC, and accessible LPT hardware; no FOD damage found. Obtained technical concurrence from CFM field service engineer on early removal recommendation. Oil sample interval reduced to every 25 flight cycles. Coordinated with airline operations to plan engine shop removal within next 100 cycles. Continuous ACARS vibration data download initiated.

description: Post-overhaul 400-cycle health assessment for Engine-05, following the successful LP bearing replacement documented in WO-10302 (April 2024). Engine-05 has completed 400 post-repair cycles with zero unscheduled maintenance events, representing a complete turnaround from its pre-overhaul deteriorating condition. Current N1 vibration is 0.19 in/s, confirmed NORMAL. Oil analysis shows iron 18 ppm, copper 8 ppm, lead 4 ppm â€” all normal baseline values with no upward trend. EGT margin 68 degrees C, indicating excellent engine health.
action_taken: Comprehensive post-repair health assessment completed: full FADEC fault history download showing no vibration faults since repair, oil sample analysis confirming normal metals trending, vibration signature baseline re-established, borescope of fan and LPC Stage 1 (both clean, no blade deterioration). Removed the thrust restriction applied during the degradation period; engine authorized for full rated thrust 100 percent N1. Health monitoring returned to standard 1000-cycle interval. Engine documented as returned to full operational health baseline.

description: High vibration detected on Comp-01 frame during monthly vibration check. Frame vibration measured at 8.5 mm/s RMS (normal less than 5.0 mm/s). Vibration spectrum showed dominant 1x and elevated 2x components, suggesting crankshaft balance or bearing issue. Vibration had increased gradually over the past 4 weeks.
action_taken: Shut down compressor. Measured all main bearing clearances. Found main bearing No. 3 (center main) clearance at 0.013 in (maximum allowable 0.010 in). Removed bearing; babbitt lining worn through to copper bond layer on lower half. Replaced main bearing No. 3 upper and lower shells; re-measured clearance 0.004 in. Post-restart vibration: 4.2 mm/s RMS.
parts_replaced: crankshaft main bearing No. 3 upper shell
crankshaft main bearing No. 3 lower shell

description: Oil leak detected on Engine-14 during pre-departure walk-around inspection. Oil trace found on underside of engine core cowl approximately 12 inches aft of fan frame rear bulkhead. Estimated leak rate 1 drop per 10 minutes. Engine oil level was 1 quart below maximum. Leak requires identification and repair before flight dispatch.
action_taken: Opened cowl access panels. Identified leak source as main oil tube B-nut fitting at LP shaft front bearing oil supply line; B-nut had worked loose due to vibration. Torqued B-nut to 75 ft-lb per AMM. Applied zinc chromate sealant around fitting. Topped up oil to maximum level. Cleaned all oil trace from cowl. Five-minute ground run performed; no leakage observed. Engine returned to service.

description: Cavitation detected on Pump-02 during overnight operator shift. Operator reported audible crackling noise from pump casing, coinciding with a 12 percent reduction in discharge pressure from normal 280 PSIG to 246 PSIG. Vibration increased from 1.8 mm/s to 3.2 mm/s RMS. Suction drum level had dropped to minimum due to upstream level control valve malfunction.
action_taken: Immediately throttled discharge control valve to reduce flow by 20 percent, lowering NPSHr and alleviating cavitation. Noise and vibration normalized within 2 minutes. Restored suction drum level by placing upstream level control valve in manual mode. After level recovery, fully opened discharge valve; pump performance normal. Impeller inspected at next scheduled outage; found minor surface pitting within acceptable limits.

description: Engine-15 LP shaft bearing deterioration has progressed significantly since initial detection in WO-10126 (June 2023). Oil analysis now shows iron at 620 ppm, copper at 195 ppm, and lead at 65 ppm. Vibration has escalated to 0.82 in/s on N1 channel. FADEC has recorded a bearing temperature exceedance: LP forward bearing thermocouple reached 185 degrees C (limit 160 degrees C). Engine-15 is now at high risk for catastrophic LP bearing failure within the next 50 flight cycles.
action_taken: Engine placed on immediate ground stop; no further flight operations authorized. Engine removal initiated. Borescope while still on wing: LP turbine area showed oil streaking from LP shaft seal, confirming bearing heat generation. Engine removed and transported to MRO shop. Full disassembly confirmed LP forward bearing with catastrophic spalling; cage had fragmented and 7 bearing balls migrated into oil system. LP shaft forward journal showed scoring. Both LP shaft and all LP bearings replaced. Full oil system flush completed.

description: Low inlet pressure alarm on Stage 1 of Comp-13. Stage 1 suction pressure measured at 10.8 PSIA, below normal atmospheric 14.7 PSIA. Reduced inlet pressure increases Stage 1 compression ratio, causing elevated discharge temperature and reduced capacity. Operator noted filter differential pressure indicator light illuminated.
action_taken: Shut down compressor. Inspected inlet air filter housing; found filter element completely plugged with dust following a recent sandstorm. Filter had been in service 3,000 hours (recommended interval for dusty environments is 2,000 hours). Replaced inlet filter element with high-efficiency 2-micron replacement. Restarted; Stage 1 suction pressure 14.6 PSIA, discharge temperature normal. Updated filter replacement interval to 2,000 hours in maintenance schedule.

description: Flow rate drop detected on Pump-06 during process performance monitoring. Flow rate decreased from design 1,400 GPM to 1,080 GPM (23 percent reduction) with no change in speed or suction conditions. Discharge pressure showed a corresponding reduction. Wear ring clearance had not been checked since the last overhaul 18,000 hours ago.
action_taken: Shut down pump and drained casing. Measured diametral clearance: casing wear ring 0.038 in, impeller wear ring 0.028 in (both exceeding maximum allowable 0.020 in). Replaced both wear rings with new 316L stainless units. Reinstalled impeller with new locknut. Verified post-installation clearances at 0.012 in. Performance test confirmed 1,385 GPM after restart, within 1 percent of design.

description: HPT blade creep suspected on Engine-06 based on elevated EGT margin deterioration rate. Engine has shown 18 degrees C EGT margin loss over the last 500 cycles, significantly above the expected 2 to 4 degrees C per 100 cycles. Creep elongation of HPT blades causes reduced turbine tip clearance and altered aerodynamics, both of which increase EGT. Engine has 4,800 cycles since last shop visit.
action_taken: Immediate borescope inspection of HPT Stage 1 and Stage 2. Stage 1 blades showed measurable tip elongation; three blades showed 0.045 to 0.060 in elongation (serviceable limit 0.040 in). Two blades exceeded the serviceable limit. Engine removed and sent to MRO facility for HPT module replacement. New HPT module installed. Post-reinstallation EGT margin confirmed restored to within 5 degrees C of new-engine standard.

description: Discharge valve failure detected on Stage 2 of Comp-09. Stage 2 discharge temperature exceeded 340 degrees F. Capacity reduced to approximately 75 percent of rated. Valve temperature monitoring showed Stage 2 discharge valves at 210 degrees F, indicating hot gas recirculation. PV card analysis confirmed loss of discharge valve sealing integrity.
action_taken: Shut down and isolated compressor. Removed all four Stage 2 discharge valve assemblies. Found two valve plates cracked through multiple rings and one spring fractured at third coil. All four discharge valve plate and spring sets replaced. Checked all seats with optical flat; all within 0.001 in flatness. Reinstalled with new O-rings, torqued to 85 ft-lb. Post-restart: capacity 998 CFM, Stage 2 discharge temperature 282 degrees F.
parts_replaced: Stage 2 discharge valve plate set (4 valves)
Stage 2 discharge valve spring set (4 valves)

description: Compressor stall event recorded on Engine-16 during climb at FL180. FADEC recorded a single compressor surge event with Ps30 pressure drop of 45 psi in 0.3 seconds, accompanied by audible bang reported by crew. Engine recovered without crew intervention. Post-event FADEC download confirmed surge event; engine continued normally for the remainder of the flight.
action_taken: Performed full borescope inspection of all 9 HPC stages. No FOD damage or blade fractures found. Inlet distortion index 8.5 percent (limit 12 percent), acceptable. Inspected VSV actuator rigging; found VSV schedule cam slightly worn, causing VSV vane angle to lag 2 degrees at intermediate power. Adjusted VSV rigging to nominal. Ground run with power transient: no surge events. Returned to service.
parts_replaced: VSV actuator cam follower roller bearing

description: Impeller wear identified on Pump-14 during scheduled 18-month clearance inspection. Wear ring diametral clearance measured at 0.023 in, exceeding maximum allowable 0.020 in. Pump had been showing gradual head loss over the past 6 months, discharge pressure declining 8 PSI from baseline, consistent with progressive wear ring clearance increase.
action_taken: Drained and removed pump casing cover. Both wear rings exceeded limits. Removed impeller and inspected vanes; minor surface roughness but no cracks or cavitation damage. Replaced casing wear ring and impeller wear ring with new 316L stainless units. New clearances: 0.012 in. Impeller balance within G2.5 specification. Performance test: discharge pressure restored to within 2 PSI of original baseline.

description: Crosshead wear discovered on Comp-06 during planned 8,000-hour overhaul. Crosshead shoe clearance (top dead center) measured at 0.024 in, exceeding maximum allowable 0.020 in. Wear is causing increased piston rod alignment deviation, potentially leading to accelerated rod packing wear and cylinder scoring. Oil analysis: copper at 85 ppm consistent with crosshead pin bushing wear.
action_taken: Removed cylinder head and piston rod from Stage 1. Withdrew crosshead assembly. Removed worn upper and lower crosshead shoes. Installed new babbitt-faced crosshead shoes and adjusted clearance to 0.010 in. Reinstalled with new gaskets. Verified piston rod alignment through full stroke; deviation within 0.001 in. Re-sampled oil at 200 hours; copper reduced to 22 ppm confirming successful repair.

description: Oil temperature high alert on Engine-11 during cruise at FL390. Oil temperature reached 148 degrees C (limit 140 degrees C). Engine at normal cruise power with ambient OAT at ISA plus 8 degrees C. Oil cooler reduced effectiveness was suspected as the root cause. ECAM oil temperature caution was active for 15 minutes before crew reduced thrust.
action_taken: Inspected fuel-cooled oil cooler (FCOC) post-flight. Borescoped FCOC core; found partial blockage in three fuel passages with carbonaceous deposits. Removed FCOC and sent to shop. Installed serviceable exchange FCOC. Ground run: oil temperature 118 degrees C at equivalent power (30 degrees C reduction). Original FCOC returned to serviceable pool after shop cleaning confirmed 25 percent improved heat transfer.

description: Motor overload trip on Pump-01 during startup from a 6-week planned maintenance outage. Motor overload relay tripped at 125 percent full-load current within 8 seconds of startup. Impeller blockage was suspected as debris may have entered during the outage period when upstream piping modifications were performed.
action_taken: Isolated and de-energized motor. Removed casing access cover. Found discharge nozzle partially blocked by a rag left in the pipeline during maintenance plus mill scale buildup from new pipe installed upstream. Removed all debris from impeller and casing. Impeller inspection showed no damage. Verified strainer basket was clean. Restarted pump; motor current normal at 98 percent FLA. Issued procedure requiring pipeline cleaning and pigging before pump restart after any pipeline maintenance.

description: CRITICAL progression of Engine-05 vibration anomaly (first detected WO-10079 March 2023, escalated WO-10231 November 2023). Vibration has now reached 0.98 in/s on N1 channel, approaching the CRITICAL threshold of 1.0 in/s. Oil metal content has deteriorated sharply in the last 50-cycle sample: iron 410 ppm, copper 180 ppm, lead 22 ppm â€” all significantly above normal limits. FADEC recorded 14 N1 speed micro-variations in the last 100 cycles. LP forward bearing failure is now considered imminent. Engine declared AOG.
action_taken: Engine declared AOG for immediate removal. Ferry flight to maintenance base at reduced thrust 88 percent N1 approved. Engine removed at maintenance base. Disassembly confirmed LP forward bearing advanced spalling: outer raceway had circumferential crack and had shed four fragments into oil system. LP shaft measured within tolerance. All LP shaft bearings (forward and aft) replaced. Oil system flushed three times with fresh oil. Engine test cell run completed successfully. Post-repair N1 vibration: 0.21 in/s.

description: PSV2 (Stage 2 discharge safety valve) lifted on Comp-14 during normal operation. Discharge pressure momentarily reached 278 PSIG, causing PSV2 (set at 275 PSIG) to open briefly. PSV reseated after 4 seconds. DCS alarm historian revealed a 3-second discharge pressure spike coinciding with a sudden spurious closure of downstream discharge control valve DCV-201.
action_taken: Reduced compressor load and confirmed system pressure stable. Inspected PSV2; valve reseated tightly with no simmering. PSV2 performance test on portable rig confirmed set pressure at 274 PSIG, full-open at 301 PSIG, reseat at 260 PSIG; valve certified serviceable. Investigated DCV-201 fast-close event; DCS logic causing spurious valve close during a specific control sequence. DCS configuration corrected by control systems engineer. Added downstream accumulator volume to absorb future pressure transients.

description: T24 temperature sensor fault recorded on Engine-20 FADEC during ground operations. FADEC logged T24 primary reading frozen at 22 degrees C for 45 minutes despite ambient temperature varying from 18 to 26 degrees C. Fault persisted through power cycle. Backup T24 channel showed normal variation, confirming primary sensor failure rather than a true temperature condition.
action_taken: Removed T24 sensor connector; connector pins showed no corrosion. Measured sensor resistance at ambient 20 degrees C: primary sensor read 215 ohms versus expected 108 ohms for Pt100 RTD, confirming internal open circuit failure. Replaced T24 primary sensor with new Pt100 RTD unit. FADEC ground test confirmed T24 channel reading 21.8 degrees C matching ambient. Engine ground run: no faults recorded.

description: Shaft seal leakage on Pump-10 identified as a continuous drip at the gland plate, approximately 25 drops per minute of hydrocarbon process fluid. This significantly exceeds zero-leakage requirement and presents an environmental and fire hazard. Pump-10 is in flammable naphtha service. Seal had been in service 19,000 hours.
action_taken: Emergency shutdown of Pump-10; transferred service to Pump-11. Locked out motor, isolated block valves, drained and purged casing with nitrogen. Removed gland plate; seal faces showed severe scoring and thermal cracking on stationary carbon face with deep erosion grooves on rotating silicon carbide face. Both faces replaced as assembly. Shaft sleeve showed corrosion pitting at 125 RMS (limit 32 RMS); replaced shaft sleeve. Installed complete new mechanical seal assembly. Zero leakage confirmed after restart.
parts_replaced: John Crane Type 1 mechanical seal complete assembly

description: Cylinder overheating alarm on Stage 1 of Comp-03. Cooling water outlet temperature from Stage 1 jacket reached 195 degrees F (alarm setpoint 180 degrees F). Discharge temperature simultaneously rose to 348 degrees F. Compressor load was not elevated beyond normal, pointing to cooling system as the likely root cause.
action_taken: Reduced compressor load to 50 percent immediately per overheat procedure. Investigated cooling water system; found Y-strainer on Stage 1 cooling water supply line completely blocked with scale and biological fouling, reducing flow from 18 GPM to 3 GPM. Removed and cleaned Y-strainer. Restored cooling water flow to 19 GPM. Cylinder temperature returned to normal within 10 minutes. Inspected Stage 1 valves as precaution; all plates intact. Added Y-strainer cleaning to monthly maintenance schedule.

description: Engine-15 returned from MRO shop following LP shaft and bearing replacement documented in WO-10382 (February 2024). This entry records the post-repair acceptance inspection and return-to-service process. Engine reinstalled on aircraft. All acceptance run parameters within limits: N1 vibration 0.24 in/s, N2 vibration 0.18 in/s, EGT margin 62 degrees C, oil pressure 58 PSIG, oil temperature 112 degrees C. FADEC fault history clear with zero bearing-related faults.
action_taken: Completed 30-minute acceptance ground run at power levels from idle to takeoff thrust with 5-minute dwell at each power setting. Vibration levels well within NORMAL band. Oil system functioning normally with no leaks. Engine logbook updated with LP shaft and bearing replacement record. Aircraft returned to scheduled service. Enhanced 100-hour monitoring plan initiated: vibration and oil analysis at each line maintenance visit.

description: High vibration detected on Pump-15 during monthly vibration survey. Vibration at pump outboard bearing measured at 5.2 mm/s RMS, exceeding the CRITICAL threshold of 4.5 mm/s. Vibration spectrum showed dominant frequency at approximately 14,400 CPM. Investigation identified the discharge nozzle pipe support as corroded and broken, allowing the 3-inch discharge pipe to vibrate freely at its natural frequency of approximately 14,200 CPM.
action_taken: Shut down pump immediately per critical vibration protocol. Transferred service to spare Pump-14. Repaired broken discharge pipe support and added an additional pipe clamp to prevent recurrence. Also re-aligned pump and motor (found 0.0035 in parallel offset). Post-repair vibration: 1.7 mm/s RMS. Scheduled full impeller inspection at next planned outage. Updated pipe support inspection to quarterly structural inspection checklist.

description: Intercooler leak detected on Comp-10 by cooling water high-makeup-water demand alarm. Cooling water makeup consumption increased from normal 2 GPH to 18 GPH over 48 hours, indicating gas-side loss. Low-level gas detected in cooling water return system confirms cross-contamination through a tube-to-tubesheet joint failure.
action_taken: Shut down compressor. Isolated both sides. Hydrostatic test of tube bundle at 225 PSIG (1.5x water design pressure); found leak at tube-to-tubesheet joint on tube No. 34 (row 3, pass 2). Attempted tube re-rolling; leak persisted. Plugged tube No. 34 with welded plug per ASME PCC-2 Article 2.9. Total plugged tubes now 3 of 96 (3.1 percent, below 10 percent limit). Reinstalled channel covers with new gaskets. Hydrostatic re-test: no leaks. Returned to service.

description: Ps30 out-of-range fault recorded on Engine-02 FADEC. HPC exit static pressure reading 168 PSIG at a power condition where normal Ps30 should be approximately 285 PSIG (48 percent below expected). Cross-check with calculated Ps30 from other engine parameters showed 278 PSIG, confirming a sensor or sense line fault rather than an actual pressure condition.
action_taken: Inspected Ps30 pressure sense line from HPC exit bleed port to transducer. Found a fatigue crack in the flexible section at the HPC casing bracket attachment point, causing pressure venting to atmosphere. Replaced cracked sense line section with new assembly. Post-installation leak test at 300 PSIG: no leaks. Ground engine run confirmed Ps30 reading 283 PSIG at same power setting, within 2 percent of calculated value.
parts_replaced: Ps30 pressure sense line flexible section

description: LPT blade damage detected during scheduled 1000-cycle borescope on Engine-08. Borescope of LPT Stage 1 revealed tip rub damage on 6 blades with blade tip shroud interlock no longer effective on 2 blades. Suspected root cause is thermal distortion of the LPT case during operations at extreme altitude with OAT of negative 62 degrees C causing momentary case constriction.
action_taken: Engineering review disposition: 4 of 6 blades within serviceable tip wear limits, 2 blades with interlock loss require replacement. Engine partially disassembled to access LPT module. Replaced 2 LPT Stage 1 blades from serviceable pool (matched pair). Verified stage 1 blade loading balance. Re-borescoped after replacement; all blades within limits. Engine ground run: no abnormal vibration or EGT spread. Returned to service.
parts_replaced: LPT Stage 1 blade assembly (qty 2 matched pair)

description: Critical oil pressure low emergency shutdown on Comp-12 during normal operation. Automatic ESD system tripped at 22 PSIG (setpoint 25 PSIG). Compressor coast-down completed normally. This is a CRITICAL fault; continued operation with low oil pressure risks catastrophic bearing failure. Oil level was at minimum graduation in the sight glass at time of trip.
action_taken: Found oil pressure relief valve stuck partially open, bypassing oil pump output back to sump. Adjusted relief valve and confirmed full seating. Also found oil filter element bypassed with bypass indicator button extended, indicating excessive filter pressure drop. Replaced oil filter element. Oil pump output test after corrections: 56 PSIG. Checked all crankshaft and connecting rod bearing clearances through inspection covers; all within tolerance. Restarted compressor; oil pressure 54 PSIG steady state.
parts_replaced: oil pressure relief valve spring and seat kit

description: Exhaust gas overtemperature CRITICAL event on Engine-19. T50 reached 638 degrees C for 6 seconds during climb to FL280, exceeding the CRITICAL limit of 620 degrees C. FADEC activated automatic thrust reduction. Crew reported a brief surge coinciding with EGT spike. EGT overtemperature inspection is mandatory before continued service.
action_taken: Performed complete EGT overtemperature inspection per AMM 77-10. Borescoped HPT stages 1 and 2: found HPT stage 1 NGV cracking at aft platform on 4 vanes and moderate TBC spallation on 6 HPT stage 1 blades; all exceeded serviceable limits. Engine sent to MRO shop for HPT module replacement. HPT module (complete NGV and blade set) replaced. LPT stage 1 inspected; minor TBC pitting within limits. Test cell post-repair: EGT margin 58 degrees C, T50 max 534 degrees C at equivalent power.
parts_replaced: HPT module assembly (NGV set plus blade set)
HPT stage 2 nozzle guide vane ring (precautionary)

description: Bearing overheating alarm on Pump-12. Bearing housing temperature reached 88 degrees C, above the 85 degrees C alarm threshold. Pump was running at normal load with ambient temperature 35 degrees C. Pump had been operating 4,200 hours since last oil change (recommended interval 4,000 hours). Extended oil service likely caused thermal oxidation and viscosity degradation.
action_taken: Shut down pump and transferred service to standby. Drained oil; found dark oil with varnish deposits. Oil analysis: viscosity 58 cSt (low end, indicating oxidative thinning), acid number 2.8 mg KOH/g (above limit 2.0), iron 45 ppm. Flushed bearing housing with flushing oil. Inspected bearings; radial bearing showed slight discoloration but no spalling. Replaced both bearings as precaution. Refilled with fresh ISO VG 68 oil. Post-restart temperature: 62 degrees C after 2-hour stabilization.

description: HP shaft bearing failure detected on Engine-13. Oil analysis at 800-cycle interval showed dramatic increase in iron (880 ppm, from 42 ppm at 600-cycle sample) and copper (310 ppm, from 18 ppm). Vibration on N2 channel rapidly increased to 1.2 in/s, exceeding the CRITICAL threshold of 1.0 in/s. Engine shut down by crew per emergency procedure during climb. Aircraft diverted to alternate airport.
action_taken: Engine confirmed CRITICAL vibration event. Grounded immediately. Borescope at diversion airport revealed no blade liberation but metallic debris in exhaust confirmed bearing failure. Engine removed. MRO inspection revealed HP aft bearing cage had fragmented; bearing balls migrated into oil scavenge system. HP shaft scored at aft bearing journal. HP shaft and all HP bearings replaced. Engine test cell run post-repair: all parameters normal. Returned to service.

description: Lube oil contamination on Comp-15 found during 1,000-hour oil analysis. Lead 85 ppm (limit 30 ppm), tin 40 ppm, copper 60 ppm (limit 50 ppm), iron 220 ppm (limit 100 ppm). Particle count ISO 18/16/13, exceeding ISO 16/14/11 limit. Elevated lead and tin indicate babbitt bearing material. Analytical Ferrography confirmed fatigue wear particles from main bearing distress.
action_taken: Shut down compressor. Drained oil and sent for Ferrography analysis. Opened crankcase inspection covers; measured all main bearing clearances. Found main bearing No. 1 (drive end) at 0.012 in clearance (limit 0.010 in). Lower shell showed severe fatigue cracking of babbitt layer over 40 percent of surface. Replaced main bearing No. 1 upper and lower shells. Flushed entire oil system three times. Replaced filter element. Refilled with fresh oil. Post-restart 100-hour sample: lead 12 ppm, iron 38 ppm. System returned to normal.
